_comment: Ground-truth ZipVoice token ids captured from sherpa-onnx with model debug on - the ids espeak-ng
produced for this sentence. Observed, not derived, which is what makes them a valid target for
"(speaking in foreign language)". ZipVoice is therefore told the clip contains words it does not, and
COMPARISONS built on it are still valid: both frontends are handed the same prompt. Its absolute word
REFERENCE CLIP: fixtures/reference/librivox-public-domain.wav - a 4.0s excerpt of a LibriVox recording,
which carries the Creative Commons Public Domain Mark. The sentence is LibriVox's standardized preamble,
so its wording is KNOWN rather than transcribed and guessed at. Peak-normalised, nothing else changed.
This replaced the packaged prompt.wav, which was paired with a transcript that is not what it says and
cost roughly six points of word error to every render, both frontends alike.
text: My daughter waited by the water for a letter from her brother.
promptText: All LibriVox recordings are in the public domain.
